t71bb_secjwl.headline: AI Detected
flagged:
AI-Generated (172 words): Write with your non-dominant hand, the clumsy one, whose letters already look like a first grader's, and let it put down whatever scared or hurt feelings are really there, nothing made up. Then your usual hand writes back as the grown-up. If talking to your little one or picturing them gets you only silence, this can get past it. And if the protective part grabs the pen first? It gets the clumsy hand until it's had its say.
If thinking things through on paper leaves you more confused, a simpler memory aid is fine. It keeps track of things without you having to work out what they mean at the same time. Looking for patterns can come later, if it's useful at all. A memory aid doesn't have to explain your life. It could be a short note of what happened, with the date, or a note of what helped. A reminder or a next step works too. Or you can leave yourself a voice note.

flagged: AI-Generated (53 words): Mornings, pick one small intention, like "Today I'll notice one hook before I act on it." At night, look back over the day. Where did you catch the hook, and where did it run its routine anyway? Then what's the next small repair, or something that'd protect your little one?
